stories.headline: ‘Wreak havoc’: US judge blocks Trump bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots
stories.bodyText:
A federal judge has rejected the Trump administration’s request to set aside up to 20,000 mail-in ballots in California over allegations that the voters may be non-citizens, warning that the move would “wreak havoc and disrupt the election that is already underway”.
US District Judge David O Carter issued the ruling on Wednesday, rejecting the Justice Department’s demand that California delay counting the ballots until the citizenship status of the voters could be verified. The decision came as more than 3.7 million people had already voted in the state, according to court proceedings cited in Associated Press (AP) reports.
“Eroded trust in our democracy is irreparable. Once a vote is segregated, lasting harm has occurred,” Carter wrote in his order.
“If the Executive can discount votes and threaten an ongoing election due to unproven allegations, then our democracy is in danger. This Court declines to be a party to such process,” he added.
Why did the court reject the request?
The Republican administration sued California election officials in mid-October, alleging that they had failed to meet a 48-hour deadline to review a list of 20,000 people whom federal authorities suspected of being non-citizens on the voter rolls.
According to CNN, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) had claimed in July that 190,000 registered California voters could be ineligible because they were foreign nationals. The government subsequently provided election officials with a list of 20,000 purported “high confidence” matches on a password-protected thumb drive and gave the state 48 hours to act.
However, local election officials found during their initial review that many names were either absent from voter rolls or listed as suspended, meaning those individuals would not receive mail-in ballots. Officials also found indications that some people identified as likely non-citizens were born in the United States, CNN reported. DHS officials disputed aspects of this assessment in court declarations.
Carter said segregating ballots at this stage would force counties to develop new procedures and risk disenfranchising voters. He also held that the request could violate the National Voter Registration Act, which restricts certain changes to voter registration within 90 days of an election.
California mails ballots to all 23 million registered voters. Court filings show more than 500,000 ballots had already been processed, with envelopes verified and ballots removed, making it virtually impossible to trace individual ballots, Los Angeles County officials testified.
The US justice department said it would immediately appeal the ruling. First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli defended the administration’s position in a social media post.
“Every day, more ballots are processed by election officials,” Essayli wrote. “This ongoing emergency disenfranchises American citizens through dilution.”
He had previously argued that segregating ballots would preserve the status quo rather than prevent votes from being counted later.
The legal dispute comes amid wider federal efforts to scrutinise voter eligibility ahead of the midterm elections, including similar litigation in Washington state.

stories.headline: ‘RSS Friends’ registers in US to step up outreach, correct inaccuracies
stories.bodyText: Washington: A group of well-wishers of the RSS has registered with the US Department of Justice as a foreign agent of the organisation with an aim to step up outreach in the US. . The RSS Friends, which provided a Georgia address in the registration document, listed Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, Keshavkunj, New Delhi as its “foreign principal”. . The RSS Friends registered with the Department of Justice under the Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) on August 27. . Correcting or responding to information that RSS Friends believes is inaccurate, incomplete, or lacking relevant context is also listed among proposed activities. . “RSS Friends does not have a written employment, consulting, lobbying, public-relations, or agency agreement with RSS containing specified deliverables, compensation, or detailed operational instructions,” the group said. .RSS plans poll outreach; to focus on SIR in UP, drug abuse in Punjab. It said the absence of a written contract should not be understood as a representation that no relationship, request, understanding, coordination, authorisation, direction, or other relevant factual connection exists. . “RSS Friends will disclose the actual facts relevant to its activities,” it said. . The group said its proposed activities are primarily informational, educational, public-relations, and community engagement activities. . “Consistent with its governing documents and applicable law, it may communicate with members of the public, journalists, media organisations, researchers, academic and policy institutions, community leaders, civil-society organisations, and, where appropriate, government agencies or officials,” the group said. . It described the RSS as an India-based volunteer and social cultural organisation. . “The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) is an unincorporated India-based body of individuals/voluntary association,” it said. . RSS Friends lists Rajendra Sonarikar, Jayant Pant and Devananda Gaddam as its Board of Directors. . Organising or participating in educational, cultural, community, or informational events; communicating, when appropriate and consistent with applicable law, with administrative entities, public agencies, or policymakers regarding factual information or perspectives concerning RSS or matters relevant to the organisation’s stated purposes is listed among the group’s proposed activities. . The registration of RSS Friends was submitted two days before RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat’s outreach programme Universal Oneness Celebration at New York’s Madison Square Garden on August 29. . The event was organised by American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue (AHEAD) Forum. PTI SKU GSP GSP

stories.headline: Karnataka High Court flags irony: Law meant to curb red tapism bogged down it
stories.deck: Karnataka Conduct of Government Litigation Act, 2023, prescribes that officers must stick to the period of limitation fixed to prefer appeals, review or revision against a court verdict, the Bench said, noting that none of the present appeals demonstrate adherence to the statutory discipline contemplated in the law
stories.bodyText:
Noticing delays from 466 days to 1,099 days in filling appeals against judgments, the High Court of Karnataka has said that the State government enacted the Karnataka Conduct of Government Litigation Act, 2023, “to arrest red tapism, but red tapism appears to have arrested the operation of this law.”
A Division Bench comprising Justice M. Nagaprasanna and Justice Hema Kulkarni made these observations on the four appeals filed by the State government challenging verdicts of a single judge related to service of certain employees in the Karnataka State Law University.
What the 2023 Act said
Apart from various judgments of the apex court on delay in filling appeals by the State authorities, the State-enacted Act of 2023 clearly prescribes that officers must stick to the period of limitation fixed to prefer appeals, review or revision against a court verdict, the Bench said, while pointing out that that none of present appeals demonstrate adherence to the statutory discipline contemplated in the law on conduct of litigation.
“The time limits prescribed for movement of files, securing opinions, and taking decisions appear to have been thrown to the winds. The State, which enacted the law to bring order and accountability into governmental litigation, has itself failed to demonstrate fidelity to its mandate. The irony is unmistakable: the State enacted a law to arrest red tapism, but red tapism appears to have arrested the operation of the law, Bench observed.
The Bench noted that the explanations offered for the delays — files moving from table to table, correspondence passing from officer to officer, legal opinions being sought and documents collected — merely chronicled administrative activity without establishing sufficient cause to condone the delay in filling of the appeal.
‘Don’t seek exception’
“The State is expected to be a model litigant, not a privileged procrastinator. Its obligation is to uphold the rule of law, not to seek exceptions from its operation,” the Bench said while observing that “a law enacted by the State cannot remain a mere ornament in the statute book, commanding obedience from everyone except its own author.
Stating that applications filed by the State government explaining reason for the enormous delay “disclose no exceptional circumstance, no compelling impediment and no credible explanation that could constitute sufficient cause for the extraordinary delays,” the Bench said, while observing that “what is presented as an explanation is, in substance, an assortment of administrative excuses; what is sought as judicial indulgence would, if granted, amount to judicial endorsement of bureaucratic apathy.”
Terming one of the applications a “verbatim reproduction” of another, the Bench said a “copy-and-paste explanation cannot become a passport to condonation of delay”.

stories.headline: Cab driver locks car, grabs woman’s arm over fare dispute in Gurugram
stories.bodyText: Gurugram: A woman travelling from Delhi airport to Gurugram in a cab has narrated a harrowing ordeal on X, accusing an Uber driver of misbehaving with her and locking her inside the car after she refused to pay more than the fare shown in the app. . Gurugram Police arrested the accused within hours of registering an FIR based on her social media post, officials said on Wednesday. . The post prompted social media users to raise concerns over women’s safety, while the police took suo motu cognisance of the alleged incident. . According to her post, the incident took place around 4.45 am after the woman arrived at Delhi airport and booked an Uber cab to her home in Gurugram. . The fare displayed on the app was around Rs 625 before the ride began. However, after the trip ended, the driver allegedly showed her a screenshot of a Rs 1,479 fare quote from Rapido and demanded the same amount. .Rapido rolls out ‘bike lift’ option amid Karnataka bike taxi row. When the woman, a software engineer, pointed out that the screenshot was from Rapido and not Uber, the driver allegedly insisted that she pay the amount quoted by the other platform. She told him that she had already paid Rs 625, according to her post. . The driver then allegedly locked the car and refused to let her retrieve her luggage unless she paid Rs 1,479. When she tried to take her belongings, he allegedly held her arm and shut the front-seat window to prevent her from removing them, she said. . The woman further alleged that after she managed to retrieve her luggage and tried to enter her house, the driver followed her, abused her, climbed the gate of her house and threatened her. . During social media monitoring, police came across the woman’s post and attempted to contact her through X, officials said. Taking suo motu cognisance of the matter, they registered an FIR and used technical assistance to identify the accused. . Teams from Palam Vihar police station and the Crime Branch, Sector 39, jointly arrested the accused, police said. . The accused has been identified as Yasir, 26, a resident of Ghasera village in Nuh district. Preliminary investigation revealed that he had created his Uber account using the name Jamil Jahid Khan, they said. . The woman had tagged Uber support in her post, seeking action against the driver and urging the company to preserve the trip and driver records. Several users also called on the platform to take immediate action. . In a statement, Uber said the alleged behaviour was deeply concerning and had no place on its platform. The company said it had removed the driver’s access to the app and was ready to assist law enforcement authorities with any information they required. . A senior police officer said strict legal action would be taken against anyone found involved in acts that threaten or compromise women’s safety. PTI COR . MDO

briefs.headline: Perfect pairing? Why India must stick with Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
briefs.deck: While Abhishek’s century was the headline act, Sooryavanshi’s fearless approach set the tone. The pair raced to a stunning 133-run stand in just seven overs, blowing New Zealand away. The Abhishek-Sooryavanshi partnership also offered a glimpse into the mindset of a new generation of T20 batters, one that sees every ball as a scoring opportunity.
briefs.bodyText:
With the T20I series against New Zealand already sealed, the pressure on India to pick the safest XI might have eased. Maybe the team management can focus on a more important question: what should India’s batting order look like two years from now, when the 2028 T20 World Cup is held in Australia and New Zealand?
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s explosive 45 off 19 balls in the third T20I in Wellington has added to India’s selection headache. It’s a happy problem. Handed an opportunity after Ishan Kishan’s injury, Sooryavanshi initially struggled at No. 3 in Christchurch as he batted outside the Powerplay. But when India pushed him up to open alongside 
Abhishek Sharma
 in Wellington, the 15-year-old was back at his belligerent best. He smashed the first ball to the boundary and never looked back.
While Abhishek’s century was the headline act, Sooryavanshi’s fearless approach set the tone. The pair raced to a stunning 133-run stand in just seven overs, blowing New Zealand away. The Abhishek-Sooryavanshi partnership also offered a glimpse into the mindset of a new generation of T20 batters, one that sees every ball as a scoring opportunity.
The innings also carried a significant subplot. To accommodate Sooryavanshi at the top, 
Sanju Samson
 willingly moved down to No. 3 despite enjoying tremendous success as opener. Since returning to the side midway through the T20 World Cup, Samson has formed one of India’s most productive opening partnerships alongside Abhishek. Together, they have scored 1,166 runs in 37 matches and become permanent fixtures at the top of the order.
Abhishek was quick to acknowledge the sacrifice. “The way Sanju bhai batted in the last game, it is not easy to let go of one’s familiar batting position. That showed his character. 
Someone’s going for his position but everyone is selfless and happy for each other, which is the hallmark of a great team,” he said in a BCCI video.
The comment revealed an increasingly important characteristic of this Indian side. Unlike previous eras where players were tied to specific positions, this Indian team, under coach 
Gautam Gambhir
, appears willing to embrace flexibility if it benefits the larger cause.
That larger cause may now involve finding out just how good a Vaibhav-Abhishek opening pair can become. The youngster himself admitted that batting at No. 3 in Christchurch had forced him away from his natural game. “Last match, I went against my grain as to how I play in T20s. This game, I wanted to give a quick start so that it becomes easy,” Sooryavanshi said.
His Wellington knock backed up that assessment. As an opener, there was visible clarity in his approach. He did not have to assess conditions or pace an innings. It was just all out attack.
Abhishek, too, felt the impact from the other end. “When Vaibhav hit the first ball, he showed aggression. I saw that at the nonstriker’s end and when you see such a shot, you also feel pumped up. Special mention and credit to Vaibhav for how he played,” Abhishek said.
The challenge now is fitting everyone into the same side when India are back at full strength. Sooryavanshi’s emergence during IPL 2026 makes it increasingly difficult to keep him on the bench. Yet India already have established performers in Samson and Kishan.
However, the debate need not be framed as Vaibhav versus Sanju or Vaibhav versus Kishan. Head coach Gautam Gambhir has repeatedly maintained that only the top two batting positions are fixed and the rest of the order remains flexible. Kishan’s adaptability strengthens that approach.
His matchwinning 80 off 46 balls at No. 5 during the Asian Games semifinal vs Sri Lanka showed he can thrive even when he is kept away from the opening slot. It also provided a possible blueprint on how all four batters can feature in the playing XI.
With the series result already decided, India can afford to think beyond just the next game.

Meet Bowen Wang: Seventh grader wins $3,500 for AI aftershock prediction too
briefs.deck: Bowen Wang, a 12-year-old student from California, has won a national technology prize for his innovative work. He created an artificial intelligence tool called Aftershock Oracle that forecasts earthquake aftershocks. This project utilized decades of data from the United States Geological Survey to make accurate predictions. Bowen's achievement highlights the potential of young researchers in…
briefs.bodyText:
A 12-year-old student from California has won a top national technology prize. He designed an artificial intelligence tool that can forecast earthquake aftershocks. Bowen Wang is a seventh-grade pupil at Central Middle School in San Carlos. He built a program called Aftershock Oracle. It predicts where secondary quakes will strike, how often they will happen, and how strong they will be after a major earthquake. His research won him the First Place Technology Award and a $3,500 prize at the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge. The Society for Science organized the contest in Washington, D.C. It is the top national science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) contest for middle school pupils across the United States.
Bowen lives in Northern California. His family’s closeness to active fault lines inspired his research. “My house is only a few miles away from the San Andreas Fault,” Bowen stated in his competition profile published by the Society for Science. “Over the past year, there have been several earthquakes that woke me up at night.” Scientists have always found main earthquakes very hard to predict. But Bowen saw that aftershocks follow clear physical patterns linked to the first rupture.
 That makes them a better fit for studying with data.
Comparing artificial intelligence models
To build the Aftershock Oracle tool, Bowen gathered decades of earthquake data kept by the United States Geological Survey. He studied quakes recorded between 1950 and 2025. He collected details about the edges of tectonic plates. He also split the first main quakes from the aftershocks that came later. He used this past data to test three machine learning models: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting, known as XGBoost. According to his project documents published by the Society for Science, all three models predicted well. But XGBoost was the most precise. Bowen put XGBoost into his own custom interface. Users can enter basic facts about a first earthquake, such as its magnitude, depth, and epicenter location. The system then gives probability-based predictions. They show where, when, and how badly aftershocks are likely to hit nearby areas. Bowen pointed out that first earthquakes make the headlines. But aftershocks create serious dangers for first responders, damaged buildings and roads, and communities trying to get people out of collapsed buildings. “They follow distinct, predictable patterns that correlate to the mainshock, making them possible to study and predict,” Bowen noted in his Society for Science profile.
National competition recognition
The Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge picks its 30 national finalists from thousands of middle school pupils. These pupils entered local and regional science fairs across the United States. Bowen reached the national stage after presenting his work at connected science fairs, including the San Mateo County Science and Engineering Fair, as shown in regional STEM network records. In the final judging rounds in Washington, D.C., a panel of professional scientists and engineers scored the finalists. They looked at scientific rigor, technical problem-solving skills, and how well each finalist could explain their work to the public. Bowen’s first-place technology award includes $3,500 to support his education and his ongoing research projects. The Society for Science noted that Bowen’s work shows how young researchers can use free, open-source earthquake data to build practical tools for public safety and disaster management.
Athletic discipline and career plans
Besides his computer science research, Bowen keeps a busy schedule outside school. He plays ice hockey and reads a great deal. “Hockey helps build mental discipline and trains me to stay focused under pressure,” Bowen shared in his Society for Science profile. He added that reading is a basic part of his daily life, stating: “Reading has redefined the way that I look at myself, and I think of it as not just a hobby, but a part of who I am.” Looking ahead, the San Carlos student plans a career in structural and civil engineering. He wants to blend modern design with protecting the environment. “One day, I will start my own firm and prove that practical, modern design and ecological responsibility can coexist,” Bowen stated in his official finalist biography. The Society for Science confirmed that Bowen and the other 2026 Thermo Fisher Junior Innovator winners will serve as ambassadors for youth STEM programs. They will encourage primary and middle school students to take on independent research projects in their own communities.

briefs.headline: Delhi-NCR wakes up to rain; IMD issues yellow alert
briefs.deck: A yellow alert has been issued for rain and thunderstorms in Delhi-NCR for Thursday and Friday. The IMD forecasts a generally cloudy sky with winds reaching 40-50 kmph during the morning. Light to moderate rainfall is expected along with possible hailstorms in the region. Residents are advised to remain cautious during thunderstorms and strong winds. The air quality in Delhi has also deteriorated…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a yellow alert for rain in Delhi-NCR on Thursday, forecasting a generally cloudy sky with spells of rain, thunderstorms and gusty winds. Isolated hailstorms are also likely over Delhi, Haryana and Chandigarh on October 29 and 30, according to the weather department.
The maximum and minimum temperatures in Delhi are expected to settle at 27 degrees Celsius and 17 degrees Celsius, respectively, on Thursday. The IMD has forecast light to moderate rainfall at several places, accompanied by lightning and gusty winds. Wind speeds could reach 40-50 kmph during the morning, while winds of 30-40 kmph are likely during the rest of the day.
The unsettled weather is expected to continue on Friday, with the IMD forecasting thunderstorms accompanied by rain. Conditions are likely to remain cloudy as the weather system brings a spell of rainfall to the national capital and adjoining areas.
The IMD's latest warning for Delhi, Haryana and Chandigarh also flags the possibility of hailstorms on Thursday and Friday. Residents have been advised to remain cautious during thunderstorms and strong winds.
Meanwhile, Delhi's air quality had deteriorated to the poor category on Wednesday, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) recorded at 229, according to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB). This was up from 197 on Tuesday, ending four consecutive days of moderate air quality.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court removes October 30 deadline for additions to Delhi electoral roll
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: In a relief to over 43 lakh voters excluded from Delhi’s draft electoral rolls for ‘permanently shifting out’, Supreme Court on Wednesday asked Election Commission not to stop adding names in the voter list by the Oct 30 deadline and told it to continue distributing and receiving enumeration forms, and Forms 6 (new voters), 7 (for deletion) and 8 (for those who shifted from one constituency to another).
A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also questioned EC on why voters whose names were there on earlier electoral rolls but were deleted from the draft rolls were asked to file Form 6, which is meant for enrolment of first-time voters.
Without passing any order, the bench said, “We will examine the issue after two weeks. The effort should be to reduce the 43 lakh (who have been deleted from draft rolls). One suggestion — publish the list of those who are deleted and specify the reason for deletion against each name. Request them to contact the nearest BLO and fill Form 8. You can give them enumeration forms. Tell them that they are welcome to fill either Form 6 or 8.”
How can you insist on Form 6 for person who was voter earlier: SC
During the proceedings on a PIL filed by activist Anjali Bhardwaj, the bench heard advocate Prashant Bhushan’s complaints against EC for insisting on filling Form 6 by those whose names got excluded and, thereby, compelling them to give a false declaration that they were first-time voters.
The bench said, “Right to vote is a vital right. If a person has shifted out from Vasant Kunj to Dwarka, or had gone out of station for a month or so and for some other reason could not respond to the EC notice or could not file the claim for inclusion of name, or did not get enumeration form because of change of address, should EC permanently disable him from voting by striking his name off the voter list?
“How can you insist on Form 6 for a person who was a voter earlier? If a person has shifted from one constituency to another within Delhi, it is erroneous to ask him/her to fill Form 6. You must allow similarly placed persons, whose names are deleted on the ground of ‘permanently shifted’, to fill Form 8.”
Appearing for EC, senior advocate D S Naidu said the commission had conducted over one lakh camps in Delhi to spread awareness among people on how to re-enter their names in the voter list.

“The situation on the ground is very different. Not a single person has come to fill Form 8. The petitioner is creating a scare on paper in the courtroom. Any person can seek inclusion of his/her name in the voter list of a constituency till the date of filing of nominations,” Naidu said, and clarified that no one has been prosecuted for using Form 6 to restore names in voter lists across states.
But EC relented to keep the window open for inclusion of names in Delhi as SC insisted that the Oct 30 deadline for filing claims and objections need not be set in stone as elections were not imminent in Delhi to warrant urgent completion of the SIR exercise.

briefs.headline: 75+ Happy Karwa Chauth messages, wishes, greetings and quotes
briefs.deck: As Karwa Chauth draws near on October 29, 2026, messages of goodwill and affection circulate among family and friends. This cherished festival fosters profound bonds through collective fasting and devotion. Tailored greetings fly between partners, relatives, and colleagues, all celebrating love. As the moon rises, the essence of unity and heartfelt expressions of care permeate the festivities.
briefs.bodyText:
Karwa Chauth has a way of sneaking up on you. One day the market stalls are piled with bangles, bindis and karwa pots, and the next you are sitting with fresh mehendi on your hands, waiting for the evening moon. Phones are already filling with greetings from mothers-in-law, sisters, friends and colleagues. Karwa Chauth falls on Thursday, October 29, 2026, in India. Puja and moonrise timings vary by city, and some calendars list October 28, so please check your local panchang. If you want your wishes to sound warm instead of forwarded, here are more than 75 messages, greetings and quotes. Send them as they are, or add a name and a shared memory to make them your own.
Happy Karwa Chauth 2026: Classic wishes for everyone
These all-purpose greetings suit relatives, neighbours and anyone on your contact list. Adding the person’s name takes only a few seconds and makes a short message feel far more sincere.
- Wishing you a blessed Karwa Chauth filled with love, patience and happiness.
- Happy Karwa Chauth! May the moon bring light and joy into your life.
- May your fast be easy, your prayers be answered and your home be full of smiles.
- Warm wishes to you and your family on this auspicious day.
- May the blessings of Karwa Mata stay with you today and always.
- Wishing you a Karwa Chauth full of faith, laughter and good food at the end of the fast.
- May every moonrise bring more love and togetherness into your home.
- Sending you festive greetings and heartfelt good wishes this Karwa Chauth.
- “Wishing you all the love, joy, and happiness in the world. May our bond grow stronger with each Karwa Chauth. Happy Karwa Chauth!”
- “May the magic of this Karwa Chauth bring us closer than ever before. May our love deepen with time. Happy Karwa Chauth!”
- "On this day of love and fasting, may our marriage grow even stronger. Wishing you a very Happy Karwa Chauth, my dearest wife."
- "Wishing you a blessed Karwa Chauth filled with the glow of the moon and the warmth of your love."
- “The moon is the same, but our love grows deeper with each passing year. Happy Karwa Chauth, my beloved wife.”
- “As I wait to see the moon, I thank God for sending you to me, and filling my life with love. Thank you for making my life so beautiful. Happy Karwa Chauth!”
Happy Karwa Chauth 2026: Messages for husbands
Many couples now keep the fast together or mark the day with a small gesture. These lines work best when they come with a thank-you, a handwritten note or a little surprise.
- Happy Karwa Chauth to the one who makes every ordinary day feel special.
-  Every Karwa Chauth, I realise how lucky I am to have you in my life.
- Thank you for being my partner, my friend and my biggest support.
- May our bond grow stronger with every moonrise. Happy Karwa Chauth, my love!
- Fasting is easy when your smile is waiting at the end of the day.
- You are the reason I look forward to every festival. Happy Karwa Chauth!
- May we always be each other’s calm, comfort and laughter.
- Grateful for you today and always. Let’s watch the moon together tonight.
Happy Karwa Chauth 2026: Messages for wives
The day is just as much about appreciation. A husband’s message, flowers or help in the kitchen can mean more than any formal greeting.
- Happy Karwa Chauth to the woman who holds our home together with love.
- Your devotion and strength inspire me every day. Thank you for everything.
- I know the day is long, so I will be here with water, snacks and a big hug when it ends.
- You look beautiful in every colour, but today you are glowing the most.
- Grateful to share my life with you. May the moon bless us both.
- Thank you for every little thing you do that no one else notices.
- Whatever the day brings, I am proud of you and grateful for you. Happy Karwa Chauth!
- You are my home, my peace and my favourite person. Happy Karwa Chauth!
Happy Karwa Chauth 2026: Wishes for mothers-in-law and elders
In many homes, the mother-in-law prepares and shares the sargi, and elders bless the fasting women. A respectful, affectionate message goes a long way.
- Thank you for the sargi, the blessings and the love. Happy Karwa Chauth, Maa.
- Your guidance has made every festival in our home special.
- Touching your feet in my heart today. Please bless our family always.
- Wishing you health, happiness and a very joyful Karwa Chauth.
- May your blessings stay with us through every fast and festival.
- Thank you for teaching us what traditions truly mean.
- Your prayers are the strongest wishes we carry. Happy Karwa Chauth!
- May you always be surrounded by love, laughter and your family.
Happy Karwa Chauth 2026: Messages for friends and sisters
Friends and sisters turn Karwa Chauth into a celebration, with matching outfits, mehendi sessions and group photos. Keep these light, cheerful and a little cheeky.
- Happy Karwa Chauth to my favourite partner in mehendi and gossip!
- May your fast be easy, your henna be dark and your selfies be perfect.
- Thank you for being the friend who makes every festival brighter.

Happy Karwa Chauth 2026: Sargi and early-morning wishes
The day begins before sunrise with sargi, a meal that sustains the fast. A thoughtful early-morning message shows you are thinking of the person observing it.
- Good morning and happy Karwa Chauth! Eat well and stay strong today.
- May the sargi give you all the energy you need to complete your fast.
- Drink plenty of water now and keep your spirits high. Sending love!
- Wishing you a calm, happy and blessed day ahead.

Happy Karwa Chauth 2026: Messages for moonrise and the evening puja
The evening is the emotional high point of the festival, with the puja thali, the karwa, the sieve and the long wait for the moon. These lines are perfect for sharing just before moonrise.
- The moon is almost here! Happy Karwa Chauth, and may your wait be worth it.
- May the moon shine on your love and fill your life with light.

Happy Karwa Chauth 2026: Quotes and thoughts for Karwa Chauth
These reflections suit captions and status updates, especially beside a photo of a decorated thali, a hand with mehendi or the moon.

briefs.headline: Isro to launch NVS-03 on Oct 30, but NavIC has a long way to go
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Isro will launch its next navigation satellite, NVS-03, aboard the GSLV-F18 rocket on Friday (Oct 30) at 11.51 pm from the Second Launch Pad at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.
GSLV-F18 is the 20th flight of India’s Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV). The mission is a crucial attempt to rebuild India’s ailing NavIC navigation constellation, which currently lacks enough operational satellites to provide standalone positioning services.
The roughly 50-metre rocket, with a lift-off mass of about 420 tonnes, will place the approximately 2,250-kg NVS-03 into a geosynchronous transfer orbit with a perigee (closest point to Earth) of 170 km, apogee (farthest point from Earth) of 37,023 km and inclination of 20.75°.
Why the launch matters
NVS-03 is the third satellite in Isro’s next-generation navigation series, designed to ensure continuity of the services of the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System, now called Navigation with Indian Constellation, or NavIC.
NavIC is intended to provide Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) services across India and up to about 1,500 km beyond the country’s landmass, reducing dependence on foreign navigation systems.
“NVS-03 carries an indigenous atomic clock alongside procured clocks and introduces the L1 signal, in addition to the existing L5 and S signals,” Isro said. The addition is expected to widen compatibility with more user devices and strengthen NavIC’s civilian and strategic utility.
But the launch comes at a time when NavIC is operating below its minimum requirement. Earlier this year, union minister Jitendra Singh told Parliament: “After completion of mission life (10 years) of IRNSS-1F, presently the NavIC constellation has three satellites — IRNSS-1B, IRNSS-1I and NVS-01 — for providing PNT services.
To provide basic positioning service, a minimum of four operational satellites are required in orbit.” The govt acknowledged that, as a result, “the NavIC constellation cannot provide standalone positioning service, however timing service is functional.”
A troubled programme
NavIC’s difficulties stem from a combination of ageing satellites, atomic-clock failures and a failed replenishment mission. IRNSS-1F completed its 10-year mission life in March 2026; soon after, Isro said its procured onboard atomic clock stopped functioning, removing the satellite from navigation service.
The more immediate setback was NVS-02, launched on Jan 29, 2025 aboard GSLV-F15. Although the satellite separated successfully and deployed its solar panels, it could not perform the orbit-raising manoeuvres needed to move from its elliptical transfer orbit to its designated circular orbit.
An Isro apex committee traced the anomaly to the spacecraft’s pyro system. It found that the drive signal did not reach the pyro valve in the oxidiser line of the orbit-raising engine, preventing the engine from firing. The committee concluded that the most likely cause was disengagement of at least one contact in each of the main and redundant connector paths.
Isro said the panel recommended corrective measures to enhance redundancy and improve the reliability of pyro-system operations, and that these recommendations have already been implemented.
Share your thoughts in the comments
Be respectful · TOI community guidelines
NVS-03’s successful launch would raise the number of navigation-capable satellites, but it will not by itself restore NavIC to full operational strength. The spacecraft must first complete orbit-raising manoeuvres, reach its designated orbit and be validated for service.
The govt has said NVS-04 and NVS-05 are in an advanced stage of realisation, meaning further launches will be needed before NavIC regains a robust, redundant constellation.
NavIC’s return to standalone positioning service depends not only on NVS-03 reaching orbit, but on Isro executing the post-launch operations that failed for NVS-02, and on the timely induction of the satellites that follow.

stories.headline: Bengaluru-based Nature Classrooms releases new butterfly migration game
stories.deck: Aswathi Asokan, who has conceptualised this new game, talks about its genesis, how it is played and how gamification can help drive conservation
stories.bodyText:
Aswathi Asokan’s journey into the fascinating world of butterflies began in 2019, as a first-year Zoology student at Chennai’s Stella Maris College. “There were a couple of professors in the Zoology Department who were interested in the natural world,” she says, recalling how one of them, Kalpana Jayaraman, was conducting butterfly walks on campus.
“So I began joining those,” says the Bengaluru-based nature educator, researcher, and conservationist who has conceptualised Monsoon Wings, a new butterfly migration and life-cycle game.
As someone who grew up on the verdant IIT Madras campus, she always loved nature, but “it had never got to the point where I was actively identifying species,” she says. Then, on that first campus walk, the professor gave participants a simple printout of the names and pictures of eight or nine common butterflies.
“That made all the difference. Every time I saw a butterfly, I would go back to the printout and try to identify it,” says Aswathi, who developed Monsoon Wings as part of her role as the manager of curriculum development, resources & training at Nature Classrooms, a Bengaluru-based organisation that works with schools and educators to connect learning and the natural world. “I like to think that this was the start of me understanding the power of a tool like that.”
She began noticing butterflies a lot more after that, closely observing their life cycles in the plants around her. At around the same time, she became part of the Chennai Young Naturalists’ Network, a group of young naturalists in Chennai.
Through this group, she met like-minded people, with whom she would go on to co-author a bilingual field guide, Butterflies of Chennai, in 2023. ”The data used to create the guide came from my friend Vikas Madhav, an experienced young naturalist who did nearly 10 years of butterfly documentation work in Chennai before moving to the US,” says Aswathi, who ended up doing a lot of nature education work in Chennai before going on to pursue a master’s in wildlife conservation action from the Bharati Vidyapeeth Institute of Environment Education and Research, Pune.
How it began
All the time spent dabbling in resource creation, including field guides, bingos and posters, has played a tremendous role in shaping this new butterfly game, which has been inspired by the ‘Bird Survivor’ game by Early Bird, an initiative by the Education and Public Engagement Programme of the Nature Conservation Foundation. “We were using this game extensively in our Nature Classrooms workshops, and I got familiar with it,” Aswathi says, explaining that this game, in turn, took inspiration from one developed by the Cornell Lab of Ornithology.
While working with Nature Classrooms, Aswathi was also actively working with Sunnyside Learning School in Chennai, running biodiversity exploration programmes for its students. “I was trying to plan a session around butterflies for the Sunnyside kids, and since the mechanics are quite similar, I thought I could adapt the bird migration game to a butterfly context and see if it works.”
While bird and monarch butterfly migration are well known and widely discussed, butterfly migration in India is so common right around us, yet few people know about it, Aswathi says. “That’s why I wanted to create a resource and incorporate that into the kids’ session.”
Aswathi first drafted the game in a text-only format, including both butterfly life cycle and migration details and adding many interesting facts about butterflies. “They go through multiple generations,” she says, adding that a lot of ecological elements of a butterfly’s life were also incorporated into the game. “In school, we learn that a butterfly goes from the egg to larva, pupa and adult stage, but there are so many other things that happen between these stages, too. So, the idea was to bring in those nuances to anyone who played the game.”
Aswathi test-drove the game, in that format, with the children she was working with back then. “I worked with elementary school kids in the age group of seven to 12. And it worked really well with them.” The exercise helped Aswathi fine-tune the game because the children came up with new questions, “which informed the later stages of development.” She also realised that the game was more than just trivia about butterflies: it allowed her to segue into getting children to think and learn about more complex phenomena plant diversity, species interactions, animal behaviour and communication.
Aswathi then shared the game with the Nature Classrooms team and conducted trial runs of it at the organisation’s educator workshop, realising that “adults enjoyed it as much as the children did.”
The final version of the game, which came out in October this year has been illustrated by Ketaki Watve. “She illustrated and designed the whole resource, while we sat down and wrote the whole natural history segment, instruction pages and all that. We wanted it to be as detailed as possible so teachers, educators, or anyone can easily pick it up, read and understand it, and then take it forward.”
About the game
Featuring four common species of milkweed butterflies —blue tiger, plain tiger, striped tiger and common crow — the game explores the massive monsoon-driven migrations these butterflies undertake annually. “This phenomenon has not been completely understood by researchers yet, but butterflies have been documented to migrate from the Western Ghats to the Eastern Ghats and back,” Aswathi says.
According to her, the game can be played by any number of people. All participants will be divided into four groups, with each one representing one of these species. The game is divided into six rounds, each one representing a particular stage of the butterfly’s journey, with different sets of cards corresponding to each round.
“If a positive event happens, the butterfly gets to flutter one or two steps forward, while a negative event results in a step back,” Aswathi says, pointing out that the team that moves the farthest forward by the end of the game is the winner. “The fun part is the action that participants get to do while moving: fluttering, laying eggs, dancing.”
After the game is over, the facilitator walks the participants through what they have learnt by asking them to describe all that happened on this journey, explains Aswathi, who has seen a huge difference in the understanding of butterfly life cycles and migration before and after the session. “Activities that are gamified really stay with people. Even if they don’t remember the entire concept, they will retain something from the session by remembering the game.”
Aswathi admits that while she had initially created it as a fun tool to use on a particular group of children, it has become a lot more than that. “It is a great way to communicate natural history to people, especially those who are just starting and learning about these things,” she believes. “Games like this really help them associate a natural history story with a fun experience, bringing in many small bits of learning. If any educator just gets children to stop and watch butterflies around them, while recalling that they migrate from one place to another in great numbers, it is still a big win for me”

stories.headline: 'Ballot' jolt for Congress: BJP-JD(S) sweeps all 4 Karnataka MLC seats
stories.deck: BJP and JD(S) successfully won all four Karnataka Legislative Council seats in the recent polls. Congress faced unexpected losses, particularly in the Bengaluru Teachers' constituency, which was previously held by them. DK Shivakumar acknowledged the results and indicated plans for corrective measures within the party. The Congress party's poor performance has been attributed to various…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: The BJP-JD(S) NDA swept all four Karnataka Legislative Council seats in polls held through ballot papers, dealing a blow to governing Congress ahead of the 2028 assembly polls.
DK Shivakumar
, facing his first polls since taking over as chief minister, said Congress would take corrective measures in view of these results. "We respect the verdict. We had expected to win two seats, but that did not happen. The Bengaluru Teachers' result, particularly, was unexpected. We will review it. Although we lost, we secured a good number of votes," Shivakumar said.
Rifts within Congress in focus
Opposition BJP mocked Shivakumar after the outcome as Congress has been demanding a switch from EVMs to ballot papers. "DK, it's done, bro! NDA sweeps all four Teachers' and Graduates' constituencies in the MLC elections," the party posted on X.
"MLC elections in 28 seats across 4 big states -- Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka. Elections held using ballot papers. Guess how many seats Congress won?" PM Modi said on X. It was an apparent taunt at Congress's continuing troubles and a rebuke to the opposition party's claim that BJP's successes are because of the EVMs and electoral rolls.
19 ministers on poll job, Cong gets 0 The polls covered 19 districts, comprising nearly two-thirds of the state, including the home districts of former CM Siddaramaiah and AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge. JD(S) candidate AP Ranganath wrested Bengaluru Teachers' seat from Congress, defeating sitting MLC Puttanna by 908 votes, while BJP won the other three seats.
In North East Teachers' seat, Shashil G Namoshi beat Sharanappa Mattur by 3,297 votes. In West Graduates' constituency, SV Sankanur posted a hat-trick of wins, beating Congress's Mohan Limbikai by 9,323, while in South East Graduates' seat, KM Suresh trounced Shashi Hulikuntemath by 23,098 votes.
KPCC president BK Hariprasad, who was also facing his first test at the hustings since his appointment, said the party will conduct a comprehensive review of its organisational and political shortcomings.
Multiple factors are said to have dealt a blow to Congress. According to party insiders, Shivakumar, despite himself being a master poll strategist, had assigned 19 ministers to oversee 133 assembly segments under the four constituencies that went to the polls, while he himself was busy with protests over SIR, Dasara preparations and his political trips to Delhi.
The failure of ministers to deliver the goods is being seen by some political functionaries as a reflection of growing differences within the party since Shivakumar became CM. Teachers' resentment over govt's failure to restore the old pension scheme may have cost Congress both the teachers' seats.
On the other hand, BJP and JD(S) showed better coordination this time around than in previous polls. In Bengaluru, BJP functionaries consolidated their party's votes behind Ranganath.

stories.headline: Ward-wise voter rolls for Bengaluru civic polls soon
stories.bodyText:
In a ray of hope for Bengaluru civic polls, the State government has directed Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) officials to extend the necessary assistance to the State Election Commission (SEC) in preparing ward-wise electoral rolls for conducting the elections.
Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said on Wednesday that the final electoral rolls following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) were published on October 27. Based on these, the SEC will have to prepare ward-wise voter rolls.
“We have told our officials that there should be no delay from our side in preparing ward-wise rolls. Our officials will extend all the assistance needed,” he said.
Subsequently, the ward-wise lists prepared on the basis of the new electoral rolls will be published, inviting objections. New additions will also be allowed during this period. After the objections are addressed, the final rolls will be published.
Mr. Gowda said these exercises would have to be completed within a stipulated timeframe, which the State Election Commission would oversee. Election dates may be announced subsequently.
A corporation commissioner told The Hindu that the SEC had written to officials earlier this month regarding training for Assistant Electoral Registration Officers and Electoral Registration Officers on preparing ward-wise electoral rolls.
“The training was also conducted in mid-October. Now, the exercise has to start,” the commissioner said.
On July 17, the Supreme Court set the end of December as the deadline for conducting the GBA civic polls. GBA officials are optimistic about meeting the deadline.

briefs.headline: Enforcement Directorate reveals Rs 10 crore deal between Sahukar and realtor in Karnataka Public Service Commission scam
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 The ongoing investigations into the alleged cash-for-job scam at Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) took an interesting turn. 
Enforcement Directorate
 (ED) sleuths told a special court that suspended KPSC chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar had carried out transactions worth around Rs 10 crore with city realtor SP Dayananda.
The revelations were made when ED sought the extension of judicial custody of Sahukar, currently lodged in judicial custody at Parappana Agrahara prison. Another accused, BV Geetha, a member of KPSC, is also in judicial custody.
According to sources, ED told the court that it had recovered handwritten account sheets from the realtor’s car.
The papers had the name and contact numbers of Sahukar. They logged Rs 5 crore allegedly received by Dayananda from Sahukar between Aug and Dec 2025, and the collective transactions between the two men aggregated to over Rs 10 crore. Also, ED explained to the court that Sahukar and Dayananda had financial transactions outside banking channels.
Sahukar and Geetha were arrested on Oct 6 in connection with the alleged leak of questions and answers for a KPSC examination held on Jan 8 and 9 for the posts of veterinary doctors.

briefs.headline: Anti-SIR coalition urges Karnataka government to reject final SIR voter list, calls for social audit and public hearings
briefs.bodyText:
SIR-Virodhi Karnataka, a Karnataka-based coalition, has urged the State government to reject the final voters’ list prepared through the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process.
Instead, a social audit, public hearings and public scrutiny of the exercise should be conducted, demanded Noor Sridhar, a leader of the Anti-SIR Coalition. He was addressing the media a day after the final electoral roll in Karnataka was published following the SIR exercise.
Mr. Sridhar, apart from demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner of India Gyanesh Kumar, said the alleged irregularities in the SIR process, claims that eligible voters had been excluded from the electoral rolls, and the impact on voting rights must be taken seriously. He urged the State government not to treat the list published by the Election Commission as final without verifying its credibility through public participation.
“For the upcoming local body elections in the State, the previous voters’ list should be used as the basis instead of the list prepared through SIR,” he demanded.
When the final list was published in Karnataka on Tuesday, 99.32 lakh names were deleted from the State’s electoral rolls. This meant that out of the 5.54 crore voters in Karnataka’s 2025 voter list, only 4.5 crore names remained in the final voters’ list.
“According to official government projections for 2026, the population of voters aged 18 and above in Karnataka is 5.19 crore. Furthermore, migration into Karnataka has been higher than migration out of the State. Given this, it is unacceptable to claim that Karnataka’s total voters are only 4.5 crore,” the coalition said, while also questioning the sharp decline in the number of voters in Bengaluru as reflected in the final list.
The coalition also raised questions about alleged wrongful deletions, reports of alleged attempts by BJP members to submit Form 7 applications in bulk, and the immense pressure on BLOs, among other issues.
“INDIA bloc is holding a protest against SIR on November 1. Taking this forward, the coalition will hold protests during the Assembly session starting on November 26,” Mr. Sridhar announced.

briefs.headline: A Hundred Hands brings river edit to Bengaluru this weekend
briefs.deck: The highlight of this edition of The Festival of Handmade is its river-themed collection
briefs.bodyText:
The Festival of Handmade by A Hundred Hands is back in the city and this time round, the works of over 200 craftsmen from as many as 26 Indian States, will be on display.
This edition of the festival is themed around the rivers of India, hence the name, The River Collection. The ethos of the festival has always been to encourage artisans to step away from the tried-and-tested and create something new; this theme has seen them use the imagery and idea of rivers as their primary motif, and the result has been an unusual range of products.
For instance, SewFabStories has a range of totes and table runners crafted from various shades and prints of blue fabric to replicate waves, while accessories from Risham Jewellery and Desi Soul are reminiscent of riverbeds and its flora. And needless to say, there is no dearth of paintings and other art work revolving around rivers.
By eliminating the middleman, the festival has closed the gap between craftsmen and potential purchasers. This method allows artisans to feel the pulse of the market, at the same time, it gives buyers a chance to express what they are interested in. Besides, by promoting handmade products, the festival encourages buyers to make socio-economic and sustainable choices.
According to a press release, Mala Dhawan, founder trustee of A Hundred Hands, says, “We chose the Rivers of India as the theme because like crafts, rivers connect people and geographies and carry stories. In this special collection, they connect different craft languages, revealing how one idea can take many unexpected forms in the hands of different makers.”
This year too, will see a fashion show hosted by fashion choreographer and stylist Prasad Bidapa, where the crafts and textiles on sale at the stalls will be showcased on the ramp, allowing buyers to see how products will appear in real time.
At the festival, one can also attend workshops on lippan work and pot painting, pottery, the building of sand terrariums, and more. Apart from open mic performances over the weekend, there will also be a flash jam on Sunday morning at 11am.

stories.headline: Oil prices slip as peace hopes ease supply fears, Middle East tensions limit losses
stories.deck: In a market shaken by geopolitical tensions, oil prices saw a downturn as traders considered possible U.S.-Iran diplomatic actions against the backdrop of supply disruption risks. Brent crude prices slipped by 0.74%, while WTI dropped by 0.89%. The recent assaults by Yemen's Houthis have further complicated the already uncertain market landscape. Mixed signals from U.S. inventory reports only…
stories.bodyText:
Oil prices declined on Thursday as traders weighed the possibility of fresh diplomatic developments between the US and Iran against the risk of further supply disruptions from escalating attacks in the Middle East.
Brent crude fell by $0.85, or 0.74%, to $114.50 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dropped $0.91, or 0.89%, to $101.90. The decline pared gains made in the previous session, when Brent advanced 1.3% and WTI climbed 3%.
The prospect of a diplomatic breakthrough emerged after US vice president JD Vance sent a letter to Iranian security council chief Mohsen Rezaei in an effort to restart peace negotiations, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing US officials and people familiar with the matter.
The possibility of further negotiations has offered some relief to oil markets, but the threat of an intensification in regional hostilities continues to weigh on the outlook for supplies. Concerns include renewed attacks by Yemen's Houthis and the possibility that the US could launch an attack on Iran after its mid-term elections on November 3.
Houthi attacks keep supply concerns alive
Fresh developments in the conflict involving the Houthis and Saudi Arabia added to uncertainty on Thursday. 
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the group said it had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired towards the kingdom's eastern region early in the day, with hostilities between the two sides showing no signs of easing.
The latest incident followed an attack on Aden airport on Wednesday, according to Yemeni government forces. A day earlier, the Houthis had said they struck Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery with a missile, escalating their attacks against the world's second-largest crude producer after the United States.
Saudi authorities had not immediately confirmed the reported strike on the refinery, which has a capacity of 550,000 barrels per day.
The continuing attacks have kept concerns over potential supply disruptions in focus even as diplomatic efforts offer the possibility of easing tensions.
Conflicting signals from US-Iran peace efforts
Efforts to find a way to end the war involving the US, Israel and Iran have produced mixed signals. An official briefed on the negotiations said Qatari mediators had presented Iran with a new draft agreement to end the conflict.
However, a senior Iranian official rejected the proposals, describing them as unacceptable ideas that did not constitute an offer.
Iran's foreign minister said on Wednesday that Tehran was continuing to give diplomacy a chance to succeed. The minister also flagged the possibility of completing Iran's seven-day plan in less than a week if it was adopted.
The contrasting positions leave the prospects for a diplomatic resolution uncertain, while the possibility of renewed negotiations has contributed to the downward movement in crude prices.
Meanwhile, US inventory data provided another factor for oil markets to follow. The US Energy Information Administration said that energy companies had withdrawn 1.9 million barrels of crude oil from storage during the week ended October 23.
Gasoline inventories, however, increased by 3.9 million barrels, against analysts' expectations of a decline of 900,000 barrels.
The opposing movements in crude and gasoline stockpiles added to the mixed signals facing oil markets as traders assessed the impact of diplomatic developments, regional attacks and US inventory data on prices.

stories.headline: Disinvestment as key economic strategy
stories.deck: Given the fact that privatisation of several PSEs is a long journey, calibrated disinvestment could serve as an interim measure
stories.bodyText:
Seven months into 2026-27, the fiscal year has been shaped by global uncertainty, high energy prices and worries over a deficient monsoon. Against this backdrop, disinvestment and asset monetisation have helped in navigating a challenging fiscal year. While receipts were already on course to meet the budget target, the government’s approval of the sale of its share in the IDBI Bank on October 14 makes it likely that the target will be exceeded. For the industry and investors, the receipts are a signal of the government’s continued commitment to reforms and a larger role for the private sector. This year so far, the disinvestment trajectory has progressed well, even before the IDBI stake sale. According to DIPAM data, the Centre mobilised ₹62,124 crore in April-September 2026 through disinvestment and asset monetisation, of which ₹55,757 crore came from disinvestment. These collections had already reached 78% of the full-year budget target of ₹80,000 crore. With the IDBI proceeds, the collections are to head past the target.
This comes at a time when the government looks to diversify its revenue sources amid rising expenditure commitments. Net tax revenue rose by a modest 3.4% in April-August 2026 and non-tax revenue by 3.2%, while capital expenditure was up by over 18%. Overall, the fiscal deficit has already reached 42% of the budgeted levels which implies a tight balance between revenue shortfalls and spending risks.
However, disinvestment should not be seen merely as a tool for meeting fiscal targets. It is a policy choice aimed at unlocking greater value from public assets, widening public ownership, and improving efficiency and governance through greater market discipline. The 2022 LIC IPO which drew in many first-time retail investors and policyholders remains a prime example.
This was precisely the rationale behind the government’s 2021 New Public Sector Enterprise (PSE) Policy which envisages a “bare minimum presence” of PSEs in strategic sectors. Likewise, the National Monetisation Pipeline (NMP) re-engines capital via mature public assets. A target of ₹16.72 lakh crore has been set under NMP 2.0 for FY26-30 after having achieved 90% of its Phase 1 goal.
Demand-based approach
This year, however, until this month, receipts had come mainly through Offer for Sale (OFS) measures which help to broaden ownership but keep the status quo on an enterprise’s operations. The strategic sale of the IDBI Bank since Air India in 2022 is an encouraging sign. From an industry perspective, the IDBI sale is more than a one-off sale. It is one of the largest Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) deals in India’s financial sector and constitutes as the first step towards a ‘Privatisation 2.0’ framework. More importantly, this framework is premised on being investor-led, professionally managed and time-bound. Two changes would help to turn into a template.
First, the selection criteria for disinvestments of PSEs should move to a demand-based approach instead of being led by the government. It would work better to first gauge interest across a wider pool and prioritise PSEs that draw strong bids at expected valuations, with structured investor feedback flagging procedural and regulatory hurdles early. Second, a rolling three-year privatisation stream, based on investor interest and the government’s strategic priorities, would give investors time for due diligence, which means deeper participation and better price discovery.
Given the fact that privatisation of several PSEs is a long journey, calibrated disinvestment could serve as an interim measure. CII analysis suggests that bringing the government’s stake down to 51% across 95 listed PSEs could fetch about ₹9 lakh crore, with the government remaining the single largest shareholder. PSEs where the government holds 75% or less could be taken up in the first two years, followed by those with higher government holdings. A dedicated body, with a ministerial board, industry experts as advisers and a management team, could steer the process.
To be sure, none of the above makes a case for fiscal complacency. Deficits and public debt tend to rise in uncertain times and stay elevated long after the shock subsides. Staying on the path of fiscal prudence is essential to ensure that the government can continue investing in health and education without crowding out private investment.
Amidst various global headwinds, a healthy progress on disinvestments with more big-ticket sales such as the IDBI will provide the Centre the required cushion to stay on course with fiscal consolidation.

stories.headline: How neoliberalism turned the world against its young
stories.deck: The rise in youth unrest stems from failures of neoliberal capitalism, which has weakened public welfare and worsened unemployment; as falling wages undermine consumption and investment, young people face fewer jobs, rising education costs and an economic system that prioritises profits
stories.bodyText:
France is in turmoil. And Albania. And Spain. Even India. As were Bangladesh or Sri Lanka earlier. The list goes on. While the specific demands may vary, one thing is common across these mobilisations: the young are on the streets. Why are the young angry the world over? In this piece, we look at the first world, in particular the G7 bloc, to understand why indeed.
France is a good example to understand what is happening in the global North. Emmanuel Macron, the antagonist according to the students in the French protests, has been in power since May 14, 2017.
Over his almost a decade-long reign, France has witnessed severe economic problems — high unemployment, low growth, rising cost of living, falling real wages and severe cutbacks in public expenditure. It is not a happenstance, therefore, that the spark that lit this protest was the lack of resources and staff at the Lycée Antoine-de-Saint-Exupéry in Créteil (a suburb of Paris).
At the heart of it all is the neoliberal economic model, which aggressively enforced reduced public expenditure in general, and welfare spending in particular. Whether it’s Macron in France or Biden/Clinton in the U.S. or Starmer in the U.K., those championing this economic model have either been ousted or are on the brink of losing power.
Crisis of unemployment
The system has angered young people in particular. Although overall unemployment rates have remained high since the pandemic, youth unemployment rates in G7 countries are now almost twice as high, if not higher (Chart 1). Generation Z (Gen Z), which has taken to the streets, comprises those born between 1997 and 2012, putting them in the 14-29 age group today. That cohort overlaps with the age group 15-29 shown in the chart.
As is well known, unlike countries in the Global South, developed countries are ageing societies, with the share of young people in their populations declining over time. Yet, as their relative population share shrinks, youth unemployment continues to rise. While fewer young people enter the labour force each year, many more join the ranks of the unemployed. Clearly, the problem is not an excess supply of labour but a lack of demand for it.
What causes unemployment?
As is the case with most economics questions, this also has broadly two sides — orthodox and heterodox. The orthodox side believes unemployment has to do with high rigid wages, inflexible labour markets, lack of a skilled labour force, most of which puts the blame, directly or indirectly, on the working class itself for its misfortune.
The heterodox side, in sharp contrast, argues it is the decision of the capitalist class to employ or not to employ workers which determines unemployment in the economy.
Consider a typical labour market — demand for labour comes from the capitalists; supply of it comes from the workers. Capitalists would like to employ as many as they could to maximise their profits. The lower the wage rate, the higher the profits, and so the demand for labour rises as wages fall (downward-sloping demand curve in graph 1). The supply curve, on the other hand, is upward sloping because as the wages rise, more workers join the labour force. The intersection of the two (point E) represents full employment — those who seek work at that wage get it.
When the economy gets stuck at point A — demand for labour (point A) is less than its supply (point B) — the economy has involuntary unemployment (equal to the gap AB). But what stops the economy from reaching point E?
Orthodox economics would tell us the wages are way too high, for which either the labour unions or rigid labour market legislation (against ‘hire and fire’, for example) are responsible. To be sure, there are other theories like the ‘efficiency wages’ which explain why the economy remains stuck at A.
The heterodox approaches argue that labour demand depends on the level of demand for goods and services in the economy. Demand, under ‘pure’ capitalism, consists of investment and consumption (see (A) in box 1). Let’s assume, for simplicity, workers consume all their wages and capitalists save their entire profits. Consumption demand would then depend on employment (wage bill), so it cannot be the cause of unemployment. The real cause, therefore, is investment. The less the capitalists decide to invest, less will be the total induced demand for goods and services, and the lower will be the need to employ workers.
It is the capitalists, not the workers, who are responsible for unemployment.
But why can the State not fill the demand gap through fiscal expansion and ensure perpetual full employment? After all, it is a win-win both for the workers and capitalists — those willing to work get work and profits rise with fiscal expansion (see (B) in box 1). That was the Keynesian route out of the capitalist crisis.
In his famous essay on ‘Political Aspects of Full Employment’, Michal Kalecki argued against this naïveté of Keynesianism because “under a regime of permanent full employment, ‘the sack’ would cease to play its role as a disciplinary measure”.
The rise of the neoliberal world order in response to the ‘New Deal’ of the 1950s and the 1960s mirrors Kalecki’s statement word for word.
Rise of neoliberalism
What was the ‘New Deal’? In response to the Great Depression of the 1930s — the deepest and the longest unemployment and profitability crisis capitalism has ever faced — a new world order emerged which argued for larger governments to push the economy towards point E. This created what is called the Golden Age of Capitalism (1945-1973), which recorded the highest ever rates of growth in the global North (see chart 2). But it came along with a class alignment in favour of the working class, whose shares in the total economic pie kept rising throughout the first world (see chart 3). The ‘sack’ was losing its role as a disciplinary measure.
A counter-revolution, led by the economist Milton Friedman, broke out, which sought to bring the ‘sack’ back. Inflation that broke out between 1973 and 1980 — the pretext of this countercharge — was cost-push (oil price shocks), and had absolutely nothing to do with larger governments. Despite that, the monetarist countercharge argued that government meddling with a ‘natural’ state of affairs under capitalism caused this unprecedented inflation. Capitalism, on its own, produces full employment and so let the markets do their job, it was argued and that governments had no business to be in business.
Ronald Reagan in the U.S. and Margaret Thatcher in the U.K. put the monetarist doctrine into practice, which has since come to be known as the neoliberal world order. With the withdrawal of the welfare state, large-scale union busting and ‘flexible’ labour markets, the balance of class forces was restored in favour of the capitalists. The share of the working class in the economic pie nose-dived and the advances of the Golden Age were reversed (see chart 3).
Crisis of underconsumption
A fall in the wage share, however, comes with its own problems. What makes sense for an individual capitalist — a fall in wage cost — harms the capitalist class as a whole, as far as profits are concerned. It happens for two different reasons. One, a dollar’s fall in wages means an equivalent fall in consumption demand, which means a fall in profits of capitalists selling these consumer goods. Two, such a fall in consumption leads to a second-degree fall in investment in the next period because why would the capitalists build more factories if the existing ones become idle? Karl Marx called it the crisis of underconsumption. Chart 3, seen together with Chart 2, is this crisis in action.
This fall in growth creates a crisis of unemployment, which is further aggravated by capital’s bid to increase its profit margins by replacing workers with machines. It is a double whammy for the youth — low growth, which is labour-displacing. Artificial Intelligence (AI) could potentially aggravate this crisis.
Last but not the least, when workers are led to believe that their lack of skills is to blame for their unemployment, they turn to education to upgrade their skills. But neoliberalism ensures that education is turned into a money-making industry worldwide.
The cost of education has been skyrocketing under the neoliberal phase (see chart 4).
Getting a degree becomes more expensive, and those who manage to get it don’t necessarily land themselves remunerative jobs. Who can blame the youth, therefore, for resisting this system rigged against them by design?
(The authors are a part of the DevMac (Development Macroeconomics) network, which seeks pluralism in Economics)
